chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Regrets: leaving Tatum for Nat; declining Oscar Peterson
summary: Collins says he should have stayed with Tatum and also should have gone with Oscar Peterson when Nat was in hospital, since Nat then stopped featuring him.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And one thing that -- you know, I don't know that I've made all the right moves in my career, but I really think that I should have stayed with Tatum. I've often

regretted leaving and going to Nat because we had started rehearsing and getting some harmonic things together that was very, very nice, you know. But I left again and tried to follow the money, which with Nat I never regretted working with Nat because Nat was -- it was just a pleasure working with him. Because in his way he was a giant also. You know.

But I think musically I would have continued to expand more, you know, being with Art, and I regretted that. And another thing that I've often wondered about is Nat was in the hospital. We had appeared at Carnegie Hall and he had an attack, and he had to have an operation for ulcers. And Oscar Peterson called me to go with him, and I said, no, I can't do it because Nat is ill and I wouldn't want to leave while he's ill, and Oscar called me two or three times. So I didn't go, Herb Ellis went with him, you know. So I thought after -- I knew that I made the wrong move there, I should have gone with Oscar because shortly after that Nat became a stand up singer and so I really had nothing play any more. And Oscar stressed playing, you see, so that I really regretted. You know. So this is just another case of making the wrong move.
